newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle feeders await next week's cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle feeders await next week's cold.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle feeders were bracing for next week's cold system which was forecast to enter the northern Plains Monday and spread south from Kansas to central Texas.
The week-long cold system could stress cattle and slow weight gains, feedlot sources said. Supplies of market-ready cattle were already tight and the cold weather could delay marketings.
Feedlots expect to price cattle from $67.00 to $68.00 per cwt next week versus $66.00 sales this week. Sources said showlists will be unchanged to smaller from this week.
"We are going to price them at $68, but realistically we will probably get to $67," said a Texas manager.

USDA confirmed comments from feedlot sources that cattle weights are dropping. In its weekly US meat production report, USDA said the average weight of cattle slaughtered under federal inspection the week ended Dec 7 was 1,169 lbs down from 1,170 the previous week and well below 1,198 a year ago.

Weather Services Corp Chief Executive Officer Peter Levitt said low temperatures next week will range from below zero Fahrenheit in the northern Plains, single digits in Kansas and sub-freezing in central Texas.
Also, the cold was expected to remain throughout the week.
Levitt said the only significant snow accumulations associated with the cold front will occur in the Great Lakes region.
However, other forecasters earlier Friday said snow was expected in Oklahoma and Kansas as well.
